diagnostics.description: Everything wrong with the composition, each a `Diagnostic` of the runtime schema.

ok.description: Whether the composition has no errors. Warnings don't count.

CheckRequest.description: The body of `POST /renders/check`. A render request is one too.

composition.description: The composition document, as `composition.schema.json` describes it.

media.description: The media manifest a render would stage, whose aliases count as present.

CompleteMultipartRequest.description: The body of `POST /media/{id}/multipart/{uploadId}/complete`: the parts to join, in order.

CompletedPart.description: One uploaded part, as uploading it answered.

CreateMediaRequest.description: The body of `POST /media`, which creates media to upload the content of.

contentType.description: 1 to 255 characters. The server decides what the file is from its bytes, not this.

sizeBytes.description: The exact size of the content to come.

cached.description:
Whether an earlier render with the same input answered the request. Always `false` on
`lumen-server`.

ErrorBody.description: The body of every error response, whatever the route.

diagnostics.description:
Each error in the composition, when it was refused as invalid. Each is a `Diagnostic` of the
runtime schema.

error.description: What went wrong, for a person to read.

media.description: The media source that failed, when one did: the runtime schema's `MediaFailure`.

ErrorCode.description: Why a request or a render failed. The listed codes are lumen-server's; another host can send others, and a render the engine failed has the engine's diagnostic code, such as `media.not_found`.

FontFace.description: One face of an uploaded font.

FrameRange.description:
The frames of the timeline a render covers, as `start..end` with `end` not included, like the
player's `range: { in, out }`. Frame numbers are the composition's, so a ranged render of frames
30 to 60 draws what a full render draws there; its output starts at time 0.

`start` defaults to 0 and `end` to the timeline's end, except for a still, whose `end` defaults
to the frame after `start`.

Health.description: The body of `GET /health`, the one route that needs no token.

version.description:
The version of this API the server implements: the `info.version` of the OpenAPI document
it follows, such as `0.6`.

Media.description: Uploaded media. A composition uses it as `asset:<id>`.

expiresAt.description: When the media is deleted, as RFC 3339 in UTC.

kind.description: What the content is, set once it was checked and readable.

metadata.description: What checking the content found, set with `kind`.

objectKey.description: Where the host keeps the file. `lumen-server` has none.

rejectionReason.description: Why the content was rejected, when `status` is `rejected`.

sourceUrl.description: The URL a `url` media was downloaded from.

uploadedBytes.description: The bytes received so far. `lumen-server` has none.

MediaKind.description: What the server decided media is by opening it, whatever its name and content type say.

MediaMetadata.description:
What checking media found. Each kind fills its own fields: images their size; video its size,
frame rate, frames, duration, codec and audio; audio its duration, rate and channels; fonts their
families and faces; environment maps their size; models their animation clips, materials and
cameras.

animations.description: The clips a `model_3d`'s `animation` selects, each the runtime schema's `AnimationInfo`.

cameras.description: The cameras a `camera` selects, each the runtime schema's `CameraInfo`.

materials.description: The materials a `texture_material` selects, each the runtime schema's `MaterialInfo`.

MediaResponse.description:
The answer to reading media, uploading its content, completing a multipart upload and
`POST /media/url`.

oneOf.description: Sent to the server, whole or in parts.
Downloaded by the server.

MediaStatus.description:
Where media is. `lumen-server` sends these three; another host can send others, such as the
hosted API's `uploaded`.

oneOf.description: Waiting for its content.
Its content was checked and can be rendered.
Its content can't be used, as `rejectionReason` says.

OutputFormat.description: The file a render writes, or for a sequence the archive of them.

oneOf.description:
A video of the frames, with the composition's audio cut to the same span: H.264, HEVC or
AV1, and AAC.
A QuickTime video of the frames in ProRes 4444, with alpha when asked for, and AAC.
A WebM video of the frames in VP9, with alpha when asked for, and Opus.

One frame as a PNG. Transparency is kept: the pixels are straight (not premultiplied)
RGBA, as the renderer's final image has it.

One frame as an opaque JPEG. Transparent pixels are composited onto black, as they are in a
video.
One PNG per frame, in one ZIP.
One opaque JPEG per frame, in one ZIP.

Render.description: A render, as creating, reading, cancelling and polling it return it.

costMicros.description: What the render cost, in millionths of a US dollar. `lumen-server` reports 0.

createdAt.description: When the render was requested, as RFC 3339 in UTC.

durationMs.description: How long rendering took, in milliseconds, once the render has succeeded.

error.description: Why the render failed or stopped, when `status` is `failed` or `cancelled`.

inputHash.description: A hash of what was requested.

outputBytes.description: The output's size in bytes, once the render has succeeded.

progress.description: From 0 to 1. Rendering fills 0.05 to 0.99, and only success reaches 1.

url.description:
Where the output downloads from, once the render has succeeded. `lumen-server`'s is
relative to the server: `/renders/{id}/artifact`.

RenderEvent.description:
A message on a render's socket, `GET /renders/{id}/socket`, named by its `type`. The socket
sends the render's current state when it opens, then each change, and closes after
`render.completed`, `render.failed` or `render.cancelled`. These are `lumen-server`'s events;
another host can send others.

oneOf.description: The render is waiting for a slot.
The render has a slot and is staging its media.
The render is drawing frames.
The render succeeded.

url.description: Where the output downloads from, as the render's `url`.

oneOf.description: The render failed.
The render was cancelled.

RenderEventType.description: The `type` of a socket event. These are lumen-server's; another host can send others.

RenderFailure.description: Why a render failed or stopped, kept with it and returned by every read of it.

media.description: The media source that failed, when one did: the runtime schema's `MediaFailure`.

retryable.description: Whether the same render may succeed when tried again.

RenderOutput.description:
What a render produces: a `format` and the `frames` of the timeline it covers. Without it a
render is an MP4 of the whole timeline.

Video quality and encoder settings are not part of it: they are the render request's own
fields, and apply to the video formats only.

jpegQuality.description: `1` to `100`, for the JPEG formats only. Unset, `90`.

alpha.description: Keeps transparency as an alpha channel, in a MOV or WebM only.

bitDepth.description: Without one the codec's default applies: 8, or 10 for ProRes.

codec.description: Without one a MOV or WebM gets its own codec and an MP4 the host's default.

composition.description: The composition document, as `composition.schema.json` describes it.

media.description: Remote media by the alias the composition uses, each an `http` or `https` URL.

output.description:
What to render: the format and the frames. Without it, an MP4 of the whole timeline.
`quality`, `codec`, `bitDepth` and `alpha` apply to the video formats only.

quality.description:
A quality preset name. Every host has `draft`, `standard`, `high` and `lossless`, and its
quality config can add others. Without one the host's default applies.

webhookUrl.description: A URL to notify when the render ends. `lumen-server` delivers no webhooks and refuses it.

RenderStatus.description:
Where a render is. `lumen-server` sends these five; another host can send others, or not all
of them (the hosted API has no `cancelled`).

oneOf.description: Waiting for a render slot.
Staging its media or rendering.
Finished, with an output to download.
Ended with an error.
Stopped on request.

RenderWebhook.description:
What a host that delivers webhooks posts to a render's `webhookUrl` when the render ends, as a
[Standard Webhooks](https://www.standardwebhooks.com) payload. The request is signed with the
`webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature` headers of that specification.
`lumen-server` delivers none.

data.description: The render as it ended, as reading it returns it.

timestamp.description: When the event happened, as RFC 3339 in UTC.

RenderWebhookType.description: Which end of a render a webhook reports.

oneOf.description: The render succeeded, and `data.url` is where its output downloads from.
The render failed, and `data.error` says why.

UploadTargetResponse.description: The answer to `POST /media`: the media, and where to `PUT` its content.

UrlMediaRequest.description: The body of `POST /media/url`, which downloads a file once and keeps it as media.

fileName.description: Without one, the URL's last path segment, or `download`.

url.description: An `http` or `https` URL, fetched through the same host checks as a media manifest.

VideoBitDepth.description: Bits per sample of a rendered video.

VideoCodec.description:
A video codec a render can ask for: `h264`, `hevc` or `av1` in an MP4, `prores` (ProRes 4444)
in a MOV, `vp9` in a WebM.
